en: Jose Rizal wrote the novel Noli Me Tangere to expose the injustices of Spanish colonial rule in the Philippines.
The Supreme Court of the Philippines, located in Manila, holds the judicial power to interpret the national Constitution.
The Philippine eagle, scientifically named Pithecophaga jefferyi, is the national bird and one of the largest eagles globally.
Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed Philippine independence from Spain on June 12, 1898, at his home in Kawit, Cavite.
The Ifugao people of the Cordilleras built the Banaue Rice Terraces over 2,000 years ago using ancient stone-walling techniques.
Fe del Mundo invented a bamboo incubator to provide affordable medical care for newborns in rural Philippine areas.
The sampaguita, scientifically known as Jasminum sambac, was declared the national flower of the Philippines in 1934.
The Baybayin script, an ancient writing system used by early Filipinos, consists of 17 basic symbols representing vowels and consonants.
The Filipino value of bayanihan refers to the traditional practice of community members working together to help a family relocate.
The Sinulog Festival in Cebu honors the Santo Niño through a rhythmic two-steps forward, one-step backward dance.
Under the Philippine Bill of Rights, every citizen is guaranteed the freedom of speech, expression, and the press.
National Artist Fernando Amorsolo is famous for his paintings depicting rural Philippine landscapes bathed in glowing backlight.
